title: A new environment with approval
scenario: "QA needs its own environment, portal-qa, by Friday. Infra changes go through the pipeline with an approval — not from a laptop." — Delivery lead (FEAT-05)
mission: Create portal-qa through Terraform and GitOps: PR plan comment, merge, pipeline apply with approval, Healthy application.
objectives: Read a plan comment before merging
Use an environment approval for apply
cost: Small extra pod requests on the existing cluster.

steps.title: Branch
steps.detail: portal-qa in local.portal_namespaces, an Argo CD Application and envs/qa values.

steps.title: Read the plan comment
steps.detail: Expect 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy for 40-aks.

steps.title: Apply with approval
steps.detail: Run infra workflow layer=40-aks action=apply and approve in the lab environment.

criteria.text: The PR has a plan comment with 0 to destroy for 40-aks
An approved deployment to the lab environment exists for the apply run
The portal-qa application is Synced and Healthy

expectedResult: A third environment created by the pipeline, with an auditable approval.

concepts.title: Plan on PR, apply with approval
concepts.body: For infrastructure, the PR shows `terraform plan` as a comment so reviewers read the exact change. After merge, the apply job runs in a protected environment that waits for a human approval — four-eyes control with an audit trail.

concepts.title: for_each vs count
concepts.body: `count` addresses resources by position (0, 1, 2): inserting an item in the middle shifts indexes and recreates resources. `for_each` addresses by key (`portal-dev`, `portal-prod`): adding a key adds exactly one resource.

example.title: reading a plan summary in CI logs
example.body: The last line of a plan is the contract you approve:
example.code: Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.

glossary.def: Gate on a GitHub environment requiring a reviewer.
How Terraform names a resource, e.g. `x.y["portal-qa"]`.

recovery: If the plan shows prod's credential being replaced, you used count instead of for_each semantics — stop.
dont: Do not apply 40-aks from your laptop
Do not merge a plan you did not read
hints: for_each addresses by key, so adding a key adds one resource.
The approval lives on the environment, not in the workflow.

interview.question: How do you make infrastructure changes safe in a team?
followUps: Where is the approval gate and why there?

debrief: Plan on PR + apply on an approved environment gives four-eyes control. for_each keyed by namespace added fic-portal-qa without touching dev/prod.

checker.plan: Read-only: gh api PR comments and run approvals, az identity federated-credential list, kubectl get application portal-qa.
